title: String Quartet No. 17 in B♭ major, K. 458 “The Hunt” — I. Allegro vivace assai
edition: PIN ONE before trusting measure numbers (e.g. NMA / Bärenreiter). Measure numbers below are authored and approximate — verify against the chosen score.
intro: Sonata form is an argument in three acts: state two ideas in two different keys (the tension), pull them apart and wander (the drama), then bring them both back in the home key (the resolution). Mozart dresses it up as a hunt. Watch the labels: the lyrical tune that first appears 'away' in the dominant returns, at the end, having made its peace with the tonic.

cues.label: First subject — the “hunt” theme
cues.listenFor: A lilting 6/8 that imitates hunting horns. The first violin sings a tonic arpeggio over a bouncing 'horn-call' accompaniment in the lower three. The galloping compound meter IS the hunt — that's where the nickname comes from.

cues.label: Transition (the modulation)
cues.listenFor: The settled tune turns restless — busier, less stable, pushing forward. This is the music leaving home: it's hauling you from B♭ toward a new key (F, the dominant). When it lands and pauses, the second idea is about to arrive.

cues.label: Second subject
cues.listenFor: A contrasting, more lyrical idea in a noticeably different key. The hunt energy softens. The whole point of the exposition is this key contrast — first idea at home, second idea away.

cues.label: Closing theme / codetta
cues.listenFor: Bright, cadential material that nails down the new key of F and rounds off the exposition before the big repeat.

cues.label: Everything you just heard, again
cues.listenFor: If this performer takes the repeat, the labels above light up a second time. The alignment step detects whether they do — many do, some don't.

cues.label: Development — the drama
cues.listenFor: Now Mozart takes the hunt motif apart — fragments tossed between the four instruments, yanked through unstable, far-flung keys. Nothing sits still. This is the 'lost in the woods' section. Near the end it parks on a tense dominant chord (the retransition), winding up to spring you back home.

cues.label: First subject returns — home
cues.listenFor: The hunt theme is back, in the home key, sounding like an arrival after all the wandering. You've heard this exact tune before — that recognition is the payoff.

cues.label: Transition — rerouted
cues.listenFor: Same bridge as before, but listen: this time it does NOT carry you off to a new key. Mozart rewrites it so it stays home. That's the structural trick of the recapitulation.

cues.label: Second subject — NOW at home
cues.listenFor: THE moment of the whole movement. The lyrical second idea that was 'away' in F the first time is now in B♭, at home. Same tune, resolved key. The argument is settled — that's what sonata form is FOR.

cues.label: Coda — sign-off
cues.listenFor: A final affirming flourish in the home key. The hunt rides off.
